{"self_assessment": "Impact: I took ownership of the upper tail (stroke 3) and laid it from the crossing through to the loop at the right end, so the fish has a clear, readable tail and the judge gets a complete fish silhouette. The body and both tails were lit up at the push, which is what makes the animal recognisable.

Execution: I started the upper tail early, laying it in steady batches from about 1:30 onward, then inspected the area twice to check it. When the chain needed extending near the loop I carried the line on with several more batches, and I confirmed the upper tail was fully in and lit before the final minutes. I then went hands-off so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I kept the table updated on where the upper tail stood, so Hana and the others always knew its status. I kept away from other people's work areas, particularly the crossing and the bottom-right corner, to avoid bumping. I backed the plan to stay hands-off at the end.

Leadership: I helped keep the mood upbeat and the team energised. I flagged the time checks and reminded everyone to keep fingers off before the push. I committed to the fish plan quickly, which let the tail strokes get started in parallel and kept the build moving.

Overall, the upper tail was a key part of making the fish read as a fish, and I delivered it reliably and on time. I'd put my share of the result at around 30 percent.", "my_share_percent": 30}
